what_its_for: Meclofenamate is a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) used to relieve pain, reduce swelling, and lower fever. It is commonly used to treat arthritis (including rheumatoid arthritis and osteoarthritis), menstrual cramps and heavy menstrual bleeding, and mild to moderate pain from other causes.
how_to_take: Take meclofenamate exactly as your doctor prescribed. Swallow the capsule whole with a full glass of water (8 ounces). Take it with food, milk, or an antacid to help prevent stomach upset. Do not lie down for at least 10 minutes after taking this medicine. Stay well hydrated by drinking plenty of fluids throughout the day.
dosing: The usual adult dose for pain is 50 mg every 4 to 6 hours as needed, with a maximum of 400 mg per day. For arthritis, the typical dose is 200 to 400 mg per day divided into 3 or 4 smaller doses. For menstrual cramps or heavy periods, 100 mg three times a day for up to 6 days is common. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions, as your dose may be different based on your condition and health history.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your pharmacist or doctor.
storage: Store meclofenamate at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medications safely out of reach of children and pets. Do not use this medicine past its expiration date. Ask your pharmacist how to safely dispose of unused or expired medication.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking meclofenamate, as it increases the risk of stomach bleeding. Do not take other NSAIDs (such as ibuprofen, naproxen, or aspirin) at the same time unless your doctor tells you to. Avoid taking this medicine if you have had a bad reaction to aspirin or other NSAIDs in the past. Avoid prolonged sun exposure, as this medicine may make your skin more sensitive to sunlight. Use caution when driving or operating machinery, as meclofenamate can sometimes cause dizziness. Tell all your doctors and dentists that you take this medicine before any procedure.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away or seek emergency help if you experience: chest pain, shortness of breath, weakness, or slurred speech (possible heart attack or stroke); black, tarry, or bloody stools or vomit that looks like coffee grounds (signs of stomach bleeding); severe stomach pain; swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat; skin rash, blistering, or peeling; yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice); unusual weight gain or swelling in your legs or feet; little or no urination; or severe headache or vision changes. Call your doctor if you have ongoing stomach upset, heartburn, ringing in the ears, or if your pain is not improving.
when_it_works: Meclofenamate usually begins to relieve pain within 1 to 2 hours after taking a dose. For ongoing conditions like arthritis, it may take several days to a few weeks of regular use before you notice the full benefit in reducing swelling and stiffness. Do not stop taking it early without talking to your doctor, even if you start feeling better.
special_populations: Older adults (65 years and older) are at higher risk for serious stomach bleeding and kidney problems with this medicine and should use the lowest effective dose for the shortest time possible. Meclofenamate should NOT be used during pregnancy, especially during the last 3 months (third trimester), as it can harm the unborn baby. Talk to your doctor before using this medicine if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Children under 14 years old should not use meclofenamate unless directed by a doctor. People with kidney disease, liver disease, heart disease, high blood pressure, or a history of stomach ulcers should use this medicine with extra caution and close medical supervision.
